metadata.title: From Meals to Marks: Modeling the Impact of Family Involvement on Reading Performance with Counterfactual Explainable AI

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the UAE 2022 PISA microdata (15-year-old students) and models reading achievement (READING) from PISA along with ten family-engagement questionnaire predictors. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight scheme, nor does it name a weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or describe complex-survey variance estimation. Because the models are standard scikit-learn regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, MLP) trained on a train/test split with 5-fold cross-validation, the analysis appears to be conducted without explicit complex-survey weighting. Analysts using the OECD PISA public-use files should consider whether to apply the provided student/sampling weights and replicate weights when estimating uncertainty, especially given the nested structure of students within schools.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analysis uses the UAE 2022 PISA dataset for 15-year-old students and focuses on reading achievement (READING) as the dependent variable. The analytic sample is restricted to cases with complete data across the outcome and the ten family-engagement predictors, because missing data were handled using listwise deletion. The dataset is then split into training (80%, n = 19,680) and testing (20%, n = 4,920) sets, with 5-fold cross-validation applied on the training set for model development and hyperparameter tuning.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 (UAE, Grade 15-year-olds) Reading achievement (READING plausible values)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Gradient Boosting (GBR) best: Test R² = 0.1879, CV R² (Mean) = 0.1882, Test MAE = 90.29, Test RMSE = 111.61. Random Forest: Test R² = 0.1342, Test MAE = 92.42, Test RMSE = 115.24. Neural Network: Test R² = 0.1876, Test MAE = 89.96, Test RMSE = 111.63.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 (UAE, Grade 15-year-olds) Reading achievement (READING plausible values) the study leveraged Family meal frequency, Time talking with parents, Discuss how school is going, Encouragement for good grades, and Parents ask about school to predict Reading achievement (READING), finding that Gradient Boosting achieved the highest predictive performance (R² ≈ 0.19) and that the strongest SHAP-ranked predictors were Family meal frequency, Time talking with parents, and Discuss how school is going. This indicates that culturally compatible, home-based family routines and parent-child communication are high-yield targets for literacy-support interventions, though the counterfactual simulations are not causal and the model explains only a modest share of reading variance.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes UAE PISA 2022 microdata for 15-year-old students (n = 24,600) to predict reading achievement (READING) using ten Likert-scale family-engagement variables. After listwise deletion of missing values, the authors train three regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and an MLP neural network) with an 80/20 train-test split and 5-fold cross-validation on the training set, tuning hyperparameters via GridSearchCV. Gradient Boosting performs best, with test R² ≈ 0.188 and test MAE ≈ 90.29 (RMSE ≈ 111.61), indicating moderate predictive power consistent with multifactorial reading outcomes. SHAP identifies family meal frequency, time spent talking with parents, and discussions about how school is going as the most influential predictors. Counterfactual simulations (univariate, holding other variables at medians) suggest large predicted score gains (baseline 358.93 up to ~448.68), but these are model-based recourse estimates rather than causal effects, and the manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights.
